source_refs.note: Topic 1.9.2, printed pages 17-18: neutral and acidic chlorides with the printed equations, and Quick Check 1.8(b, c) as the self-check.

blocks.text: Chlorine forms chlorides with other elements, and these show characteristic behaviour in water, giving solutions that are acidic or neutral.

items: Neutral chlorides: salts that dissolve in water to give a neutral solution with a pH close to 7. At the start of period 3 the chlorides of sodium and magnesium do not react with water; their solutions contain the positive metal ions and negative chloride ions surrounded by water molecules, now known as hydrated ions, and the process is hydration. NaCl(s) gives Na+(aq) + Cl-(aq), pH 7; MgCl2(s) gives Mg2+(aq) + 2Cl-(aq), pH 6.5. The group 1 and group 2 chlorides are neutral, with few exceptions.

Acidic chlorides: from aluminium to sulfur in period 3 all the chlorides react with water to make acidic solutions with pH below 7, a process called hydrolysis. When AlCl3 is added to water, the hydrated Al3+ ion causes a water molecule to lose an H+ ion, which turns the solution acidic: AlCl3(s) + 3H2O(l) gives Al(OH)3(s) + 3HCl(aq). Other examples: SiCl4(l) + 2H2O(l) gives SiO2(s) + 4HCl(aq); PCl3(l) + 3H2O(l) gives H3PO3(s) + 3HCl(aq).

blocks.prompt: Why is AlCl3 an acidic chloride while NaCl is not, and would PCl5 and NCl3 be acidic or basic?
blocks.explanation: Sodium chloride simply dissolves: its ions are hydrated and the solution stays neutral. The small, highly charged Al3+ ion pulls an H+ off a water molecule, hydrolysis, releasing HCl and making the solution acidic. PCl5 and NCl3 are covalent non-metal chlorides, so they too hydrolyse in water to give acidic solutions; neither is basic.

items: Neutral chlorides (NaCl pH 7, MgCl2 pH 6.5) only hydrate. Acidic chlorides from Al to S hydrolyse, releasing HCl: AlCl3 gives Al(OH)3, SiCl4 gives SiO2, PCl3 gives H3PO3, each with HCl.
